symptoms: Dark brown to black necrotic spots with characteristic concentric rings (target-board appearance)
Yellowing chlorotic halo surrounding lesions on older foliage
Premature leaf drop and senescence starting from lower canopy upwards
Tomato___Early_Blight.cause: Fungal pathogen Alternaria solani thriving in warm temperatures (24-29°C) accompanied by heavy dew, frequent rains, or overhead irrigation.
immediate_actions: Prune and safely destroy lower infected leaves showing target-like spots
Discontinue overhead watering immediately to prevent leaf moisture persistence
Sterilize pruning shears with 70% isopropyl alcohol between plants
management: Foliar application of Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2.0 g/L at first visible lesion appearance
In cases of rapid disease progression, rotate with systemic Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1 ml/L or Difenoconazole 25% EC @ 0.5 ml/L
Repeat application at 7-10 day intervals during humid cloudy weather
prevention: Adopt a 2-3 year crop rotation cycle with non-solanaceous crops like maize or legumes
Apply organic straw or plastic mulch around plant bases to prevent soil-splash inoculation
Ensure proper plant spacing (60 cm x 45 cm) for optimal air circulation within canopy
monitoring: Inspect lower canopy leaves every 3-4 days for concentric target spots
Monitor canopy humidity and leaf wetness duration following rainfall events
Tomato___Early_Blight.disclaimer: Fungicide recommendations are provided for educational guidance. Follow local agricultural extension rules and label instructions. Consult a certified agronomist for severe outbreaks.

symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked pale green to dark brown lesions on leaf edges and tips
Delicate white fungal-like downy sporulation on the underside of leaves in moist morning conditions
Rapid foliar browning, collapse, and blackened water-soaked petioles and stems
Tomato___Late_Blight.cause: Oomycete Phytophthora infestans favored by cool temperatures (15-20°C) with prolonged relative humidity (>90%) and continuous leaf wetness.
immediate_actions: Immediately rogue out and destroy severely blighted plants to prevent rapid spore dispersal
Halt all overhead sprinkler irrigation and reduce field moisture levels
Erect physical barriers or treat adjacent unaffected blocks with protective fungicide shield
management: Spray Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5 g/L water thoroughly covering both leaf surfaces
For curative knockdown during outbreaks, apply Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.0 g/L or Dimethomorph 50% WP @ 1.0 g/L
Apply copper oxychloride 50% WP @ 3.0 g/L as a protective barrier in early season
prevention: Plant certified disease-free transplants and blight-resistant hybrids (e.g., Arka Rakshak)
Avoid planting tomatoes adjacent to potato fields
Ensure adequate field drainage to prevent waterlogging and persistent ground humidity
monitoring: Daily inspection of leaf undersides during cool, cloudy, or fog-prone mornings
Track regional disease alert forecasts from local agro-meteorological stations

symptoms: Severe upward curling, puckering, and crinkling of apical leaves
Pronounced interveinal chlorosis, pale yellowish margin, and thickened leaf lamina
Stunted bushy plant stature with shortened internodes and extensive flower drop
Tomato___Leaf_Curl_Virus.cause: Tomato Leaf Curl Begomovirus transmitted persistently by the silverleaf whitefly (Bemisia tabaci).
immediate_actions: Uproot and burn virus-infected plants early to eliminate vector virus reservoirs
Install bright yellow sticky traps @ 15-20 traps per acre to monitor and reduce whitefly population
Spray cold-pressed Neem oil (10,000 ppm) @ 3 ml/L as an eco-friendly vector repellent
management: Control whitefly vectors with systemic insecticides: Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.5 ml/L or Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 0.3 g/L
Alternate with Spiromesifen 22.9% SC @ 1.0 ml/L or Diafenthiuron 50% WP @ 1.0 g/L to combat vector resistance
Apply foliar micronutrient blend with zinc and boron to mitigate viral stress on unaffected growth
prevention: Plant barrier crops (2-3 dense rows of maize, sorghum, or pearl millet) around the tomato perimeter
Raise nursery seedlings under 40-mesh insect-proof nylon net covers
Select ToLCV-tolerant cultivars such as US-440, NS-501, or Arka Ananya
monitoring: Check underside of tender apical leaves weekly for whitefly nymphs and adults
Monitor yellow sticky trap catch counts twice weekly

symptoms: Spindle-shaped or diamond-shaped lesions with grey or whitish centers and brown margins on leaves
Lesions enlarge and coalesce, causing complete foliar drying and scorched appearance
Collar rot and dark necrotic nodal lesions under severe infestation
Paddy___Rice_Blast.cause: Magnaporthe oryzae fungus favored by high relative humidity (>90%), prolonged leaf wetness (dew), and excessive nitrogenous fertilizer application.
immediate_actions: Immediately suspend top-dressing of nitrogenous fertilizers
Maintain optimal water layer in paddy fields to reduce blast susceptibility
Isolate severely blasted nursery beds with protective fungicide barrier
management: Foliar spray of Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6 g/L or Isoprothiolane 40% EC @ 1.5 ml/L
Alternatively, apply Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC @ 1.0 ml/L at first appearance
Repeat spray 10-12 days later if favorable weather persists
prevention: Seed treatment with Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 2 g/kg seed or Carbendazim 50% WP @ 2 g/kg seed
Avoid excessive and unbalanced application of urea; apply nitrogen in 3-4 split doses with potash
Adopt blast-tolerant varieties recommended by ICAR / regional agricultural university
monitoring: Scout nursery and tillering stage crops weekly, especially after overcast rainy days
Inspect leaf blades in early morning for spindle-shaped lesions

Paddy___Brown_Spot.cause: Fungal pathogen Bipolaris oryzae typically prevalent in nutrient-deficient (especially potassium, manganese, and silicon) or water-stressed soils.
immediate_actions: Correct water stress and ensure consistent field moisture
Apply potassium and micronutrient foliar sprays to boost plant defense
management: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1 ml/L
Apply Carbendazim 12% + Mancozeb 63% WP (Saaf) @ 2 g/L during active tillering
Ensure uniform canopy coverage with adequate spray volume (200 L/acre)
prevention: Perform seed treatment with Thiram 75% WP @ 3 g/kg seed before sowing
Incorporate balanced fertilization based on soil testing, ensuring adequate potash application
Amend zinc and silicon deficiencies in nursery and main field
monitoring: Inspect seedling and vegetative stages weekly for brown oval lesions
Check soil moisture and nutrient status regularly

Cotton___Cotton_Leaf_Curl.cause: Begomovirus transmitted by the whitefly (Bemisia tabaci); spreads rapidly under hot, dry spells interspersed with humid conditions.
immediate_actions: Rogue out and bury severely curled plants in early vegetative stage (<60 DAS)
Install yellow sticky traps @ 20 traps/acre at crop canopy height
Eradicate alternate weed hosts (Abutilon indicum, Parthenium) around field borders
management: Control whitefly vectors with Pyriproxyfen 10% + Clothianidin 5% EC @ 1.5 ml/L
Alternate with Flonicamid 50% WG @ 0.4 g/L or Afidopyropen 50 g/L DC @ 2 ml/L
Avoid synthetic pyrethroids which induce whitefly resurgence
prevention: Cultivate CLCuD-resistant Bt cotton hybrids approved by regional research institutes
Synchronize sowing in the block to avoid staggered vector breeding
Grow 2-3 rows of pearl millet or sorghum as vector barrier
monitoring: Scout top 3 leaves of 20 random plants weekly for whitefly counts and vein clearing
Trigger control when whitefly ETL reaches 6-8 adults/leaf

Potato___Late_Blight.cause: Phytophthora infestans favored by cool temperatures (12-18°C), continuous high humidity (>90%), and rainfall/fog.
immediate_actions: Rogue out and destroy infected vines immediately to prevent tuber wash infection
Hill up soil properly to protect developing tubers from spore wash
Stop sprinkler irrigation
management: Apply protective Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 3 g/L before disease onset
At first appearance, spray Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Dimethomorph 50% WP @ 1 g/L
Alternate systemic fungicides to prevent pathogen resistance development
prevention: Plant blight-resistant potato varieties (e.g., Kufri Girdhari, Kufri Jyoti)
Use certified disease-free seed tubers and pre-sprout them
Practice dehaulming (cutting vines) 10-12 days before harvest to avoid tuber contamination
monitoring: Daily inspection of crop canopy during cool foggy or rainy periods
Watch for blight forecast alerts from regional agro-meteorological units
